thread:
sara_sales: Hey team — Vendem kickoff tomorrow. They want a Private deployment POC but are unsure between VPC peering vs PrivateLink. They asked for a firewall/egress checklist and any pricing delta we should flag. Can infra/security weigh in?

raj_infra: Short answer: both can work, tradeoffs: peering is straightforward if they control both VPCs and want full L3 routing. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is better if they need strict isolation & don’t want route-table changes. Non-transitive peering is a gotcha for multi-account setups.

emily_security: From a security questionnaire POV: PrivateLink reduces attack surface because traffic doesn't go over the public internet and can be restricted per ENI. It also avoids adding routes and potential accidental exposure. But we need to confirm their egress firewall can reach our endpoint IPs (or allow DNS to resolve our endpoint).

matt_se: For pricing: call out that PrivateLink has an endpoint hourly charge + per-GB data processing on AWS. VPC peering avoids an endpoint hourly fee but you should warn about inter-AZ/data transfer costs and the ops complexity if they have many accounts. For POC, peering is usually cheaper to spin up quickly; PrivateLink is preferred for long-term enterprise deployments.

sara_sales: Great. Can you give a minimal firewall allowlist (IPs/ports) and a quick connectivity test command we can send to Vendem's infra team? They are on-prem -> TGW -> spoke VPC to us.

raj_infra: Minimal suggestions:
- Outbound 443 (TLS) to our managed endpoint DNS name (we provide DNS hostnames).
- If they insist on IPs: allow our egress IP CIDR block: 34.198.0.0/16 (example) — NOTE: for PrivateLink they will connect to ENI IPs inside their VPC, so no public IPs are needed.
- For VPC Peering: ensure route table entries for the peer and allow ephemeral high ports for TLS if firewall restricts by port ranges.

raj_infra: Quick curl test (run from a linux box in their spoke VPC):
```
# resolves endpoint and tries a TLS handshake
curl -v -o /dev/null -s "https://redwood-vendem.private.redwood.example/v1/health" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redwood-test-token>"
```

emily_security: Also ask them to provide a packet capture if the curl fails (SYN/RST or TLS alert) and confirm their DNS resolves our service FQDN to the interface endpoint (PrivateLink) or public hostname (hosted).

matt_se: POC checklist to include in the email:
- Which connectivity mode they want (Peering vs PrivateLink)
- IAM role or cross-account permissions for PrivateLink (if we need to accept the endpoint service connection)
- Expected QPS and peak concurrency (for sizing Dedicated vs Hosted for cost estimate)
- Test window (we can be on-call during 09:00-11:00 PT Thu 03/26)

sara_sales: They also asked about SLA & data residency. Can we note anything short?

emily_security: SLA depends on deployment: Hosted has our standard API SLA, Dedicated includes reserved capacity SLAs, Private (customer-managed) means SLA/DR is mostly on the customer's infra but we provide control plane support. For data residency, confirm the region and whether logs/metrics go to our control plane or their VPC (we can offer optional metrics forwarding into customer account).

raj_infra: Technical blocker to flag: if their firewall only allows fixed destination IPs and they refuse to allow DNS-based endpoints, PrivateLink may still require them to allow ENI CIDRs inside the VPC — which they control — but if they're expecting a single static public IP for outbound to Redwood hosted endpoints, that won't be stable for hosted. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can provide static egress IPs on request (extra network config) — but that needs Sales/SE to sign-off on extra engineering steps.

matt_se: I'll draft the email with pricing bullets: quick POC estimate (no reserved): approx $X/day for hosted testing (token usage dependent), PrivateLink adds ~per-hour endpoint cost + per-GB processing (callout), Dedicated requires a capacity commit — I'll include ranges and ask for QPS to refine.

sara_sales: Perfect. Action items:
- @matt_se: draft the POC email + rough estimate by EOD.
- @raj_infra: prepare an operations checklist + sample curl and traceroute commands.
- @emily_security: short blurb for the security questionnaire about PrivateLink peering and logs.

infra-test-bot: NOTE: scheduled connectivity window set for 2026-03-26 09:00-11:00 PT. Please confirm participants.

sara_sales: Confirmed, I'll loop in Vendem infra (cc: vendem-netops) and send our checklist. :thumbsup:

matt_se: Draft sent to thread, drop any edits and I'll forward.

raj_infra: One more tip — if they use TGW and multiple spokes, remember that PrivateLink endpoints are per-VPC; peering/IGW/TGW routing may need NLB/endpoint service changes. Keep the initial POC to a single spoke to reduce complexity.

sara_sales: Thanks all. I'll update the deal tracker with the chosen approach after the POC kickoff.
